name: National Palace Museum
funding: A state agency under the Executive Yuan, Taiwan's cabinet. The Legislative Yuan froze NT$350 million for renovation in December 2024 and over 20 percent of the 2025 budget.
watch: Visits fell from 6.14 million in 2016 to 2.87 million in 2024 across both branches; Hsiao Tsung-huang has been director since January 2023.

propaganda.summary: Opened by the KMT government in 1965, the museum served to assert the KMT's legitimacy as the sole legitimate Chinese government and to educate Taiwanese about their Chinese heritage.

name: Anıtkabir (Atatürk Mausoleum and Museum)
funding: The General Staff of Turkey's armed forces, in control since the 1980 coup, runs it as a military installation with free entry. A 1981 law declared it a national monument.
watch: The mausoleum, built from 1944, opened in 1953 and its museum in 1960; 6,550,480 visitors in 2024, 1,092,000 of them on 10 November alone.

propaganda.summary: Run by the Turkish General Staff since 1980, Anıtkabir presents an authorized version of Turkish history; official visits and ceremonies honour Atatürk and the Republic, re-sacralising the Atatürk cult.

name: Panorama 1453 History Museum
funding: Owned and run by Kültür A.Ş., the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality's culture company, which built it from 2005 and opened it in January 2009. Financed by the municipality and ticket sales.
watch: Built at Topkapı where the Ottomans breached the walls in 1453; opened after three years with praise from Prime Minister Erdoğan.

propaganda.summary: The AKP-run Istanbul municipality's Kültür A.Ş. opened it in 2009 to convey the spirit of the 1453 conquest; Posocco (2018) analyses it as a case of AKP-era museums promoting Ottoman and Islamic nationalism.

name: Iñupiat Heritage Center
funding: Owned and run by the North Slope Borough as a National Park Service affiliated area. The borough pays for more than 90 percent of its budget with taxes on oil and gas infrastructure.
watch: Public money, but the borough's revenue rests on Prudhoe Bay and other North Slope oil fields.
records_note: The borough publishes its budget books; no line for the centre was read.

name: National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War
funding: A state museum financed from the state budget under the Ministry of Culture, which renamed it in July 2015 under the decommunisation laws. Its director general is Yurii Savchuk.
watch: The 102 metre Motherland Monument houses the main exhibition; in 2023 the Soviet emblem on its shield gave way to the Ukrainian trident.

propaganda.summary: Opened in 1981 by Leonid Brezhnev as the Ukrainian State Museum of the History of the Great Patriotic War, beneath a Motherland statue bearing the Soviet emblem, to commemorate the Soviet war narrative.

name: State Museum of the History of the Temurids (Amir Timur Museum)
funding: A state museum under the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan, built under Cabinet Resolution 99 of 14 March 1996 and rebuilt under a presidential decree of 5 February 2026.
watch: The building with a blue cupola, modelled on Samarkand's Gur-e-Amir, faces the Timur statue; President Mirziyoyev reopened it on 9 April 2026 with interactive exhibits.

propaganda.summary: Karimov's government built the museum for Timur's 660th anniversary in 1996 as a centrepiece of the state Timur cult. It displays the Ideology of National Independence and Karimov portraits; Mirziyoyev reopened it in 2026.

name: Cuartel de la Montaña 4F (Chávez Mausoleum)
funding: State-owned, controlled by the Ministry of Defense and the Bolivarian National Militia, based there since 2008. The state organises visits and an honour guard watches the sarcophagus.
watch: Built 1904 to 1906 in 23 de Enero. Acting president Delcy Rodríguez renewed her oath at the tomb on 6 January 2026 after Maduro's capture.

propaganda.summary: After Chávez died in March 2013 the Maduro government turned the barracks of his 1992 coup into his mausoleum and museum, with honour guard, daily cannon salute and state-staged narrative placing him beside Bolívar.

name: Ho Chi Minh Museum
funding: A public service unit under Vietnam's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, which by Decision 2372/QD-BVHTTDL of 2025 sets its propaganda and education tasks and lets it collect fees.
watch: Founded by a 1970 Party resolution and opened 19 May 1990, Ho Chi Minh's centenary, in Garon Isacovich's lotus-shaped building; over 40 million visitors.

propaganda.summary: Created by Communist Party resolutions of 1970 and 1977 and opened in 1990, the state museum is tasked by ministerial decision with propaganda and education on Ho Chi Minh's thought and revolutionary ideals.

name: Vietnam Military History Museum
funding: Run by the defence ministry and the army's General Department of Political Affairs under the Central Military Commission; the state funded the 2,500 billion dong building, opened in November 2024.
watch: A 64,640 square metre building on a 74 hectare site with a 45 metre Victory Tower and over 150,000 artefacts, four of them national treasures.

propaganda.summary: The army's General Political Department built the new museum, opened in 2024 to honour the People's Army and its defence tradition. Party chief To Lam called it a red address for studying the Party's leadership.

name: War Remnants Museum
funding: A public institution of the Ho Chi Minh City government under its Department of Culture and Sports, funded from the city budget and ticket income.
watch: Opened 4 September 1975 at 28 Võ Văn Tần; about 500,000 visitors a year, two thirds of them foreigners.

propaganda.summary: Opened by the new communist authorities on 4 September 1975 as the Exhibition House for US and Puppet Crimes, renamed in 1990 and 1995; anthropologist Christina Schwenkel describes its uncontextualised self-representation of American war crimes.
